structural_evidence.fact: Central facade has six giant Ionic columns spanning the middle facade; projecting north/south end bays make a recessed centre.
Two north/south roof pavilions with semicircular arch heads; modified Mansard roof.
Stone bases and columns, cement faux-stone walls, baroque relief decoration; varied square/round/semicircular/triangular door-window forms.

photo_observation.observed: Six Ionic columns divide five central full-height window bays; one broader window bay in each projecting end pavilion. Upper central arcade appears as five groups of three narrow arched windows (15), plus a large arched window in each end pavilion. Towers are open belvederes with corner posts, arched pediments and domed caps; roof has dormers.
photo_observation.confidence: main columns/bay layout high; small upper-window grouping medium (perspective photo, not measured drawing)
photo_observation.not_verified: Metric dimensions of cornice, roof ridge and tower crown.

structural_evidence.fact: Primary entrance lies on Guangdong Road; east/north street facades both articulate the prominent site; NE corner has an inward-curved corner face.
Single NE roof pavilion, paired columns on its four sides and an Islamic-influenced gourd-shaped cap.

Floors 1,2,3,5 generally rectangular windows; floors 4,6 semicircular-headed windows. Black cast-iron balcony railings at selected 4th and 6th floor bays; Baroque cornice, pilaster and arch decoration.
Steel-framed building, granite exterior cladding, large open office spans. Horizontal facade tiers comprise ground floor, floors2–4, floors5–6.

photo_observation.observed: Chamfered/curved corner entrance below stacked balconies; broad projecting cornice above fourth floor; paired top-floor arched windows separated by pilasters; pavilion has tall narrow openings/paired supports and a gourd finial. Ground arches in current photograph differ from generic text claim of rectangular ground windows; follow actual photograph for modeled visible facade.
